body:
GitHub issue #395 (P0, security). Fleet's model-plane worker runs with NO filesystem isolation, under the operator's real HOME, with repo-authored `fleet.gate` commands in its permission allowlist and a charter that tells it to run them. Candidate-authored code therefore executes with the operator's filesystem privileges.

## Attack path (each link verified against 07b49f78)

1. `packages/fleet/lib/config.mjs` takes `gate` from the CANDIDATE tree's `.adlc/config.json` (`gate: config.gate ?? null`) — unlike `adapter`/`adapterCommand`/`adapterArgs`/`model`, which are operator-local.
2. `packages/fleet/lib/adapters/claude-code.mjs` `buildSettings()` maps `gate.build`, `gate.test`, `config.init`, and `allowedCommands` into `Bash(<cmd>)` allow rules in the worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json`.
3. `packages/fleet/lib/charters.mjs` `builderPrompt()` instructs: "Run the gate commands yourself before finishing."
4. `packages/fleet/lib/live-deps.mjs` `dispatch()` calls `adapter.dispatch({ exec: io.spawnWorker })` directly — NOT through `Sandbox`. Only the repo-command plane uses `sandboxFor(worktree)`.
5. `packages/fleet/lib/env-scrub.mjs` `modelPlaneEnv()` keeps `HOME` verbatim and EVERY `ADLC_*` var (`isAdlcControl`), including `ADLC_QUARTERMASTER_REGISTRY` — handing the worker the absolute path of the operator-local channel registry.

Result: a candidate commits `fleet.gate.test = "node tools/gate.mjs"`; that script rewrites the quartermaster registry with a schema-valid document routing frontier work to weak supply. The current run's seats are snapshotted, but the NEXT run — and any resume, which re-plans seats from the registry as it is at resume time — loads attacker-chosen supply. Nothing downstream looks wrong.

The registry is not uniquely exposed: `~/.claude` settings and hooks, harness credentials, the installed toolkit, and other repos' worktrees are all reachable by the same path.

## Design

Isolate the model plane's FILESYSTEM while preserving its NETWORK egress. The two are independent; the K2 rationale in `docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` §7.3 only requires the latter.

- `packages/fleet/lib/sandbox.mjs` already has a `mode`/`backend` abstraction with a synthetic-home bind and read/write/network predicates. Add a `network: 'deny' | 'allow'` profile axis rather than a new mechanism.
- Route `live-deps.mjs` `dispatch()` through a model-plane `Sandbox` (network allowed, writes bounded to the worktree + a model-plane home).
- Adapters declare the auth material their harness needs, so it can be exposed READ-ONLY and nothing else is. This is a natural companion to the `aliases`/`forcesModel`/`transports` capability metadata the catalog already carries.
- `modelPlaneEnv()` must stop passing operator-local absolute paths (`ADLC_QUARTERMASTER_REGISTRY` and any sibling) to the worker. Dispatch resolves seats BEFORE the worker starts, so the worker never needs the path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An end-to-end test in which a repo-controlled command run on the model plane attempts to overwrite an operator-local registry file OUTSIDE the worktree asserts the file's bytes are UNCHANGED after the run. The test runs for real when a sandbox backend is detected on the host and reports a skip (never a silent pass) when none is.
   Verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/model-plane-sandbox.test.mjs`.
2. The same containment proof for a write to a synthetic `$HOME/.claude/settings.json` outside the worktree.
   Verify: same file.
3. A test asserting the model-plane env contains NO operator-local registry path — `ADLC_QUARTERMASTER_REGISTRY` is absent from `modelPlaneEnv()` output even when present in the source env — and that the withholding is expressed as a rule over a NAMED SET of operator-local vars, so a sibling var added later is withheld by construction rather than by another enumerated case.
   Verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/env-scrub.test.mjs`.
4. A test proving network egress is PRESERVED on the model plane: the model-plane profile's `networkAllowed` predicate is true, the bubblewrap argv carries no `--unshare-net`, and the Seatbelt profile does not deny network — while the repo-command profile still denies all three. Without this the fix silently breaks every run.
   Verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/sandbox.test.mjs`.
5. Behaviour when no sandbox backend is available on the model plane is explicit and tested: the model plane reuses the run-wide sandbox decision, so a host with no backend either refuses to dispatch or runs under the operator's existing `--i-am-in-a-disposable-container` assertion. No new silent-degrade path is introduced.
   Verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/model-plane-sandbox.test.mjs` asserting the refusal and the override path.
6. `docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` §7.3 updated: K2 currently justifies the worker being outside the sandbox ENTIRELY; it must justify being outside the NETWORK sandbox while inside a FILESYSTEM one.
   Verify: read the section; `npm test` (spec/docs consistency checks) passes.
7. The threat-model text added by T151 updated — `docs/integrations/quartermaster-registry.md` ("Threat model — and its documented limit") and the `quartermaster` toolkit page callout — to state what now holds and what does not.
   Verify: read both; the interim wording "not selected by the candidate, not unreachable by it" no longer stands unqualified.
8. Any residual limit (a platform whose backend cannot express part of the profile) is stated in the spec and in the threat-model docs rather than left implied.
   Verify: read the spec section.

## Non-goals

- Restricting model-plane egress to a per-provider endpoint allowlist. §7.3 aspires to it; this ticket keeps egress open and closes the filesystem half only.
- Hardening resume against a mid-run registry swap via `registryDigest` acknowledgement. That is attestation-schema-v2 work (spec §9 item 4); fixing the filesystem hole removes the hazard without changing resume semantics.
- Reworking the repo-command plane's existing profile.
title: Contain the model plane: filesystem-isolate the fleet worker while preserving provider egress (#395)
